first: locked out of my apt and it's 11pm. help

tenant.situation: You stepped out to take the garbage down and the door locked behind you. Your keys and phone charger are inside; you have your phone.

knows.spare: nobody else has a key; your roommate is away until Sunday
knows.stove: nothing is on inside, no pets
knows.safe: you're in the hallway, you're fine

doesnt_know: whether the manager has a spare key tonight

truth.problem: Tenant locked out of the unit at night.

judge: Checks quickly that nothing dangerous is left on inside and that the tenant is somewhere safe.
Gets the lockout to the manager fast and explains any after-hours fee policy honestly without inventing amounts.

first: le verrou de ma porte d'entrée est super dur à tourner

tenant.situation: The deadbolt on your front door is very stiff to turn with the key and from the inside knob. It locks, but you have to force it.

knows.what: the key turns only with a lot of force; the thumb-turn inside is also hard
knows.door_open: with the door open the bolt turns more easily
knows.cold: it started when the weather turned cold

doesnt_know: whether the bolt rubs the strike plate
tenant.style: writes only in French, casual, short messages

truth.problem: Deadbolt binding on the strike plate (door shifted slightly); adjust strike and lubricate.

judge: Asks whether it turns easily with the door open, which points to the strike plate rather than the lock.
Warns not to force the key so it doesn't break off, and suggests only a dry/graphite lubricant if any.

first: key stuk in the door wont come out

tenant.situation: Your key is stuck in the front door lock. It turned and the door is unlocked and open, but the key won't pull out.

knows.key_position: it's turned partway; it won't go back to straight
knows.door: the door is open and you're inside
knows.key_state: the key looks a bit bent

truth.problem: Bent key stuck in a lock cylinder not returned to the vertical position.

judge: Gives the safe step first: turn the key back to the straight position and wiggle gently while pulling, not force.
Points out the door can't be locked while the key is stuck and sets priority accordingly.

tenant.situation: The keypad on your front door smart lock doesn't light up or beep when you press the numbers. You are outside the unit.

knows.what: no lights, no beep when you press keys
knows.before: for a few days it beeped differently and flashed red
knows.key: you have a physical backup key at work, not with you
knows.tried: pressed every button, held the lock logo

doesnt_know: whether there is a 9V emergency contact
tenant.style: writes only in simplified Chinese, short messages

truth.problem: Dead batteries in the smart lock keypad (low-battery warning ignored).

judge: Recognises the earlier red flashing as a low-battery warning and mentions the 9V emergency contacts or backup key if the lock has them.
Since the tenant can't get in, treats it as a lockout for the manager rather than only giving battery tips.

first: my front door won't lock at all

tenant.situation: The deadbolt on your front door won't go into the frame when the door is closed, so you can't lock the door. It's evening.

knows.where: your unit's front door, ground floor
knows.what: the bolt comes out fine when the door is open but hits the frame when it's closed
knows.latch: the handle latch holds the door shut but doesn't lock
knows.frame: the metal plate on the frame looks a bit lower than the bolt; the frame by it has a crack
knows.alone: you live alone and feel unsafe tonight
knows.tried: pushed and pulled the door while turning the key

truth.problem: Deadbolt misaligned with a cracked/shifted strike area of the door frame; the unit can't be locked.

judge: Treats an unlockable ground-floor door as urgent and gets it to the manager the same day.
Offers a safe stopgap for tonight (use the latch, a door wedge, chain) and records the cracked frame.

first: someone smashed my window, i think they got in. stuff is moved

tenant.situation: You just came home and found the ground-floor bedroom window smashed and things moved inside. You don't know if anyone is still there.

knows.when: you just walked in a minute ago
knows.glass: broken glass on the floor and the sill
knows.inside: drawers open in the bedroom; you haven't checked the other rooms

doesnt_know: whether the intruder is still inside

truth.problem: Break-in through a smashed window that just happened; intruder may still be inside; window must be boarded and secured.

judge: First tells the tenant to get out to a safe place and call 911 because the intruder may still be inside, before any repair questions.
Alerts the manager urgently to board up and secure the window, and doesn't ask for photos or for the tenant to clean up.

first: sliding door to the patio doesnt lock anymore

tenant.situation: The sliding glass door to your ground-floor patio closes but the latch won't catch, so it can be slid open from outside.

knows.where: living room sliding door to the ground-floor patio
knows.what: you flip the lock lever but the hook doesn't grab; the door slides open
knows.gap: when closed there's a small gap at the latch side at the bottom
knows.track: the bottom track has some dirt and pebbles
knows.tried: pushed it hard closed and flipped the lever; worked once

doesnt_know: whether the rollers or the latch are worn

truth.problem: Sliding door doesn't close fully (dirty track / worn rollers) so the latch hook misses the keeper; door can't be secured.

judge: Suggests clearing the track and closing the door fully, and offers a dowel or bar in the track as a stopgap so it can't be slid open.
Flags that a ground-floor door that won't lock needs prompt attention.

first: lost my keys yesterday, can i get a new set? how much is it

tenant.situation: You lost your keyring with the unit key, the building fob and the mailbox key. You can get in because your partner has a set.

knows.what_lost: unit key, building fob and mailbox key on one ring
knows.address_on_keys: no tag or address on the keys
knows.access: your partner has a full set, so you're not locked out
knows.want: a new set; you wonder if the lock should be changed

doesnt_know: whether the fob can be deactivated

truth.problem: Lost keys and fob; manager issues replacements, deactivates the fob and decides on rekeying. Not a repair.

judge: Says the manager will arrange replacement keys and the fob, and that the cost depends on the manager, without inventing a price.
Notes that the fob was lost too so it can be deactivated, and doesn't send the tenant to a locksmith on their own.
